domains.question: When cities adopt extreme-heat alerts and heat action plans, what evidence distinguishes the practical heat exposure and access barriers of vulnerable residents, epidemiological heat-health risk estimates, and actual implemented programs or independently measured health improvements?

modules.title: Unequal daily heat exposure and cooling access
modules.summary: Practical problem: exposure of low-income urban residents, older adults, outdoor workers, and people without effective cooling; distinctions in place, lived experience and access

modules.title: Attribution and measurement of heat-related health harm
modules.summary: Academic evidence: heat exposure, excess morbidity or mortality, vulnerability confounding, urban heat islands and measured health risk

modules.title: Heat alerts, cooling centers and heat health action plans
modules.summary: Program layer: proposed measures, officially documented operations, cooling-center accessibility and whether observed outcomes were actually evaluated

domains.question: In informal electronic waste recycling, how do documented worker and community exposure problems, academic studies measuring lead or other toxic exposures, and government/institutional collection or safety programs connect—and which interventions have measured outcomes rather than only proposed actions?

modules.title: Unsafe informal e-waste processing and community exposure
modules.summary: Practical problem: informal burning, dismantling and occupational exposure including communities around informal recycling sites; region-specific source observations

modules.title: Biomonitoring and scientific assessment of e-waste toxicants
modules.summary: Academic evidence: measured lead, other heavy metals or pollutants and health outcomes, exposure routes, study design limitations and causal identification

modules.title: Formal e-waste collection and worker protection initiatives
modules.summary: Program layer: safe collection plans, recycling guidance, documented implementation, occupational protections and independently evaluated exposure reductions
